Jadow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Jadów, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are first recorded in Jadów in the 18th century; by 1921, 1,492 Jews made up over 75% of the village's population, most murdered at Treblinka in September 1942. The cemetery's exact founding is unknown, though synagogue records confirm burial-fee income by 1851 at the latest. In 1942, 100-200 victims of the Treblinka deportation were buried here in a mass grave; the Germans later had the bodies exhumed and burned. Postwar survivors marked and memorialized the mass grave, though metal fencing around it was later stolen and its Holocaust monument destroyed. Fewer than 100 tombstones or fragments survive today, with only about 20 intact. In 2012, a symbolic tombstone was unveiled for Sarah Litvak, who had died the year before in Chicago - a rare instance of a memorial connecting the site to a specific diaspora descendant.
